definition.stemRaw:
A strategy manager reviews a Claude-generated recommendation to merge the company’s two regional warehouses into a single location. The recommendation references three sources estimating cost savings and one source that confirms consolidation is operationally feasible. Two source documents also include estimates of one-time transition costs and a stakeholder concern about regional service levels, neither of which is included in the recommendation.  
  
Which concern is most justified?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The recommendation is acceptable for an initial round, but the missing material should be added in a separate appendix rather than reprompting the original output.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The recommendation reflects selective use of the source documents and should be re-prompted to address the transition costs and the service-level concern before it is used.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The recommendation should be rejected because it relies on only four sources, which is insufficient for a decision of this size.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The recommendation is sound because every source it cites supports the consolidation conclusion.

definition.explanation: A decision recommendation must account for material evidence that could affect the outcome. Omitting documented transition costs and a concern about regional service levels presents only the favorable evidence for consolidation, so the recommendation should be re-prompted to address those issues before it is used.

definition.stemRaw:
You are an operations lead classifying proposed Claude use cases according to whether they are acceptable for your team to pursue.  
  
Which two proposed use cases are acceptable for the team to pursue with Claude? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer provides a complete solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: synthesizing themes across approved customer feedback under aggregation rules

choices.label: B
choices.text: summarizing performance review notes across a team to support a manager’s promotion decisions

choices.label: C
choices.text: drafting a preliminary symptom summary to support a clinician’s diagnostic review

choices.label: D
choices.text: drafting a legal summary that an attorney will review and edit before sharing with a client

choices.label: E
choices.text: drafting an internal training summary from approved internal documentation

definition.explanation:
Synthesizing approved customer feedback under aggregation controls and creating internal training summaries from approved internal documentation are bounded, low-risk information-processing tasks. Promotion decisions are employment-related high-impact decisions, while diagnostic support and client-facing legal drafting involve healthcare and legal guidance, respectively; these domains require heightened safeguards and are not routine team-approved use cases merely because a human reviews the output.

**Learn more:** [Anthropic Usage Policy Update](https://www.anthropic.com/news/usage-policy-update)

definition.stemRaw: You are an analyst tackling a one-off, complex problem that truly requires multi-step reasoning across an extended chain of thought. Which model is most appropriate for this work?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A non-Anthropic model, because the Claude lineup has no option for complex reasoning.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Opus, because it is positioned as the most capable for advanced reasoning on complex specialized tasks.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Haiku, because lightweight models are always preferred regardless of complexity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any model, because reasoning depth does not vary across the lineup.

definition.explanation:
Opus is Anthropic’s highest-capability model tier and is positioned for advanced reasoning and complex, specialized tasks. That makes it the appropriate choice when a one-off problem requires an extended, multi-step reasoning process.

**Learn more:** [Intro to Claude](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/welcome)

definition.stemRaw:
Before uploading a customer file for Code Execution analysis, a customer-success associate at Noventra, Ltd. is reviewing the planned task.  
  
Which two practices most closely align with sound data handling? (Choose two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Confirm that the planned Code Execution task aligns with the organization’s data classification policy and escalate to the appropriate contact if the data sensitivity exceeds approved use.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Review the file for sensitive, confidential, or regulated fields before upload, and remove or redact any fields that are not required for the planned Code Execution analysis.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Skip the upload review entirely on the basis of urgency, even though the file might contain regulated fields that organizational policy requires the user to redact before any code execution.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bypass the data classification policy because the task is internal, treating sandboxed processing as an exemption from the review the policy requires before sensitive data is uploaded.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Upload the full unredacted customer file without review, on the assumption that a sandboxed execution environment removes the need to apply the organization’s data classification policy.

definition.explanation: Data should be handled according to the organization’s classification policy, with escalation when the planned use exceeds approved sensitivity limits. Files should also be reviewed before upload so that sensitive, confidential, or regulated fields not needed for the analysis are removed or redacted. A sandboxed execution environment does not eliminate these policy and data-minimization obligations.

definition.stemRaw:
You are assessing proposed workflow changes to determine whether they materially improve the workflow. Which two proposed changes meaningfully improve a recurring Claude workflow? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer provides a complete solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: updating the team’s shared workspace name to reflect the new workflow process

choices.label: B
choices.text: labeling each workflow step with descriptive names to improve readability for new team members

choices.label: C
choices.text: extracting the standard reference material into a Project to avoid repeating it

choices.label: D
choices.text: reorganizing the workflow document’s section headings to improve navigation

choices.label: E
choices.text: adding a quality check on outputs before they enter the downstream process

definition.explanation:
Claude Projects use uploaded knowledge as context across all chats in the Project, so placing standard reference material there avoids repeatedly supplying the same context in a recurring workflow. A quality check before output enters a downstream process prevents incorrect or unsuitable results from being propagated. Workspace names, step labels, and document headings improve organization or readability but do not add reusable Claude context or an output-control mechanism.

**Learn more:** [How can I create and manage projects?](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9519177-how-can-i-create-and-manage-projects) · [Understanding Claude's personalization features](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10185728-understanding-claude-s-personalization-features)

definition.stemRaw: You are evaluating a Claude-generated report that maintains a confident tone throughout. Which question most effectively distinguishes plausibility from verification?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Can each specific claim be traced to a credible source or to the supplied input material?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Does the response open with a clear, well-framed statement of the main finding?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Does the response cover the topic comprehensively based on its length and section count?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Does the response use varied sentence structure across sections?

definition.explanation: Verification requires checking whether individual claims are supported by credible sources or by the supplied input material. Confidence, framing, length, coverage, and sentence variety can make content seem plausible but do not establish that its claims are substantiated.

definition.stemRaw:
You are a marketing manager determining what to put in custom instructions for a writing-focused Project.  
  
Which two items should be included in the custom instructions? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer provides a complete solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: the brand voice and the tonal expectations the writing must follow

choices.label: B
choices.text: a representative sample of past writing that reflects the team’s preferred style and structure

choices.label: C
choices.text: the prompt author’s preferred response length for internal messages unrelated to external deliverables

choices.label: D
choices.text: the preferred writing style of the marketing manager who will review all final deliverables

choices.label: E
choices.text: the standard structure and the length expectations for typical deliverables

definition.explanation:
Writing-project instructions should set the reusable requirements that apply to the project’s outputs, including the brand voice and tonal requirements, as well as the standard structure and expected length of typical deliverables. Project instructions can direct how ChatGPT responds within that project, including style, concision, and formatting.

**Learn more:** [Projects in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-using-projects-in-chatgpt)

definition.stemRaw:
You are a knowledge worker who broke a “draft a board memo” request into fifteen small steps and noticed that the output now feels disjointed because related ideas were separated.  
  
Which adjustment is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Combine the original request back into one unstructured sentence.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Subdivide each tiny step into ten more tiny steps for additional precision.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Remove all sequencing so the steps run in random order.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Consolidate related steps into fewer cohesive sections that group naturally connected ideas.

definition.explanation: Related work should be consolidated into cohesive sections so naturally connected ideas remain together, improving coherence without discarding the useful structure of the task.

definition.stemRaw: You are a knowledge worker reviewing a Claude-generated brief that claims a “well-known industry standard” but does not identify any source. How should this claim be handled?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Treat the assertion as unverified, and either source it from an authoritative reference or remove it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Accept the assertion because the phrase "well-known" is reassuring.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Republish the brief unchanged because the claim sounds authoritative.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Strengthen the assertion by adding more confident wording.

definition.explanation: Claims about an industry standard require support from an authoritative, identifiable reference. An unnamed assertion remains unverified and should be sourced or removed rather than accepted or strengthened based on its wording alone.

definition.stemRaw:
You are breaking down a “build a customer journey map” request.  
  
Which sequence of decomposed steps is correct?  
  
1. Identify the touchpoints the customer experiences during each stage.  
2. Define the persona and the journey scope that will be mapped.  
3. Document pain points and opportunities at every touchpoint.  
4. Synthesize the findings into the finished journey-map artifact.  
5. Identify the primary stages the persona progresses through.
definition.explanation: A customer journey map is grounded in a defined persona and journey scope. Its structure is then established by identifying the persona’s major stages, followed by the touchpoints within those stages. Pain points and opportunities are evaluated at those touchpoints before all findings are synthesized into the final journey map.

definition.stemRaw: A knowledge worker is using the AI Fluency Framework’s Description competency to revise an underperforming prompt. Which revision most accurately reflects Description principles?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Remove the existing context from the prompt and submit only the bare task statement, eliminating the audience, format, and constraint information that Description principles call for in a clear specification.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Replace the specific instructions with generic phrasing that broadens the task scope, undoing the specification work that Description principles require for a reliable, useful output on the next run.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Specify the task scope, the required output format, the audience, and the relevant constraints with sufficient clarity that the prompt produces a useful, reliable output on the next run.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add length to the prompt by inserting filler text that does not specify task scope, output format, audience, or constraints, leaving the original specification gaps in the underperforming prompt unaddressed.

definition.explanation:
Description involves communicating goals clearly enough to prompt useful AI behaviors and outputs. Defining the task scope, required output format, intended audience, and applicable constraints provides the specification needed for a useful, reliable result.

**Learn more:** [AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations](https://www.anthropic.com/ai-fluency/overview?_bhlid=b8c18e03b1a33b4448fd0488e89cafa0e5db4c14) · [The AI Fluency Framework](https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/b383cf6baddbfc72fdf8b0ed533a518e2872d531.pdf)

definition.stemRaw:
You are a knowledge worker moving from a long, drifting conversation to a fresh, focused session. What is the correct sequence of transition steps?  
  
1. Start a new chat and paste the summary as its initial context.  
2. Summarize the goals, key decisions, and open questions from the lengthy conversation.  
3. Determine which references should remain available beyond the current chat.  
4. Place persistent references in a Project’s knowledge base or attach them as needed.  
5. Verify that the new chat is on-task before resuming the work.
definition.explanation:
A focused continuation requires a usable summary before a new chat can receive its starting context. References intended for reuse should be identified and added to Project sources or attached before continuing, because Projects keep related chats, files, and instructions together to preserve context and stay on-task. The new chat can then be validated for alignment before work resumes.

**Learn more:** [Projects in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-using-projects-inchatgpt)

definition.stemRaw: An operations assistant is redesigning a recurring data-processing workflow step to use Code Execution. Which two design decisions best promote reliable integration? (Choose two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Vary the input file format from run to run to accommodate the different source systems that supply the data each week.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Define a brief output verification step in which the human reviewer confirms the computed result against an expected range or sanity check before the output advances to downstream consumers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Embed the Code Execution step inside the workflow without documenting the expected output format or the fields it produces.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Standardize the input file format the step expects, so each run of the Code Execution step receives consistent input and produces comparable, verifiable output across recurring weekly cycles.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Eliminate the human review step that follows Code Execution, since the sandboxed environment already verifies that the code ran without errors.

definition.explanation: Recurring automated processing is most reliable when each execution receives a consistent input structure, allowing outputs to be compared and verified across cycles. Successful code execution only establishes that the code ran; it does not establish that the computed result is valid for the business context. A human reviewer’s expected-range or sanity check provides a control before downstream consumers receive the output.

definition.stemRaw:
You are assessing proposed evaluation criteria for a Claude-generated business brief. Which two criteria are valid for evaluating a brief produced by Claude? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer represents part of the solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: factual accuracy of the claims made against the supplied source material

choices.label: B
choices.text: consistency of the writing style with the organization’s established tone guidelines

choices.label: C
choices.text: total word count of the output relative to industry benchmarks for business briefs

choices.label: D
choices.text: presence of an executive summary section as a structural completeness check

choices.label: E
choices.text: alignment of the output with the requested format and length constraints

definition.explanation:
A reliable evaluation of an LLM-generated business brief measures factual grounding against the supplied material and task fidelity to the requested output requirements, including format and length. These criteria are specific, measurable, and directly relevant to the brief’s intended use.

**Learn more:** [Define success criteria and build evaluations](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/develop-tests) · [Reduce hallucinations](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-hallucinations)

definition.stemRaw:
You are a member of an operations team preparing input to summarize customer feedback. The feedback file combines public quotations with personal contact information.  
  
Which preparation method is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Extract only the feedback content needed for the summary, redact or anonymize personal contact details, and submit the trimmed input.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Submit the entire file unchanged so Claude has complete context.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Replace the feedback content with the personal contact details and ask Claude to invent the missing feedback.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Strip out the feedback content and submit only the personal contact details.

definition.explanation:
Only the feedback necessary for the summary should be provided, while personal contact details should be removed, redacted, or anonymized. This preserves the information needed for the task while minimizing unnecessary exposure of personally identifiable information.

**Learn more:** [Customer Support Agent — Claude Platform Docs](https://docs.anthropic.com/de/docs/about-claude/use-case-guides/customer-support-chat)

definition.stemRaw: You are an operations lead and observe that a Project’s outputs have been drifting away from the team’s current expectations. Which maintenance action should be attempted first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Review the Project’s instructions and reference materials against current standards.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Switch the Project to a different Claude model in the hope it behaves better.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Continue using the Project and accept the drift as the new baseline of behavior.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Retire the Project and rebuild a new one from scratch with fresh content.

definition.explanation:
Project instructions define how Claude should behave and respond across the Project’s chats, while uploaded project knowledge supplies the shared context. Reviewing those instructions and reference materials against current standards addresses the most direct, controllable cause of output drift before considering a model change or rebuilding the Project.

**Learn more:** [How can I create and manage projects?](https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/9519177-how-can-i-create-and-manage-projects) · [What are projects?](https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/9517075-what-are-projects)

definition.stemRaw: A manager is determining which changes to make during a memory-maintenance review for a long-running workflow. Which two actions most effectively support memory quality over time? (Choose two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Delete all memories as the maintenance action to ensure a clean slate, then allow Claude to rebuild context organically through subsequent workflow runs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Disable Memory entirely to eliminate the risk of stale entries surfacing in future workflow runs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Identify and edit or delete entries that are stale, inaccurate, or no longer relevant, and add context Claude has not automatically captured but the workflow continues to need.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Leave all memories untouched on the basis that the workflow has been running consistently and no output quality issues have been reported.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Export the current memories as a backup before making changes, so prior context can be restored if a maintenance edit unintentionally removes information the workflow still depends on.

definition.explanation:
Effective memory maintenance includes reviewing and updating stored context so it remains current, accurate, and useful; obsolete or incorrect entries should be edited or removed, while necessary missing context should be added. Backing up existing memories before changes provides a recovery path if an edit accidentally removes context the workflow still requires. Anthropic’s memory guidance recommends regularly reviewing and updating memory as projects evolve.

**Learn more:** [Manage Claude Code memory](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/memory)

definition.stemRaw:
An HR business partner is creating a long-running workspace in which a team handbook, a leveling guide, and a policies-FAQ document will be used across many separate chats by several team members.  
  
Which Claude feature is intended for this use case?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Connect the team’s Google Drive folder where the three documents live, so the connector surfaces them inside each chat at the moment the chat needs them.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Generate an Artifact containing the three documents, which gives the team an editable surface for the reference content that persists across chats.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a Project, which provides a persistent workspace with its own knowledge base and custom instructions shared across chats and members.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Attach all three documents to each chat as needed, since per-chat attachments give the chat direct access to the documents without additional setup.

definition.explanation:
Claude Projects provide a persistent workspace with a project knowledge base whose uploaded content is used across chats within that project. Projects can also be shared with other organization members on Team and Enterprise plans, and project instructions apply to all chats in the project.

**Learn more:** [How can I create and manage projects?](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9519177-how-can-i-create-and-manage-projects) · [What are projects?](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9517075-what-are-projects)

definition.stemRaw: You are an analyst verifying facts in a Claude-generated report. Two cited sources provide conflicting dates for the same event. Which approach is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Choose the more recent date on the basis that later sources typically reflect updated or corrected information.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Average the two conflicting dates and use the average.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Locate a primary or authoritative source for the event and use the date that source confirms.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Publish both dates without resolving the conflict and let the reader choose.

definition.explanation: A primary or authoritative source is the strongest basis for establishing an event date and resolving a conflict between cited sources. Recency alone does not establish accuracy, dates cannot be meaningfully averaged, and an unresolved conflict should not be presented as verified fact.

definition.stemRaw:
A business analyst is transforming a stakeholder’s sticky-note request into a structured prompt for Claude. What is the correct sequence of conversion steps?  
  
1. Confirm the audience and the decision that the response needs to support.  
2. Submit the structured prompt to Claude.  
3. Identify the underlying task concealed in the sticky-note language.  
4. Specify the required length, tone, and output format.  
5. Add the supporting facts and constraints that are relevant to the task.
definition.explanation:
A useful structured prompt progresses from the underlying task and intended audience or decision to the relevant context and constraints, followed by explicit output requirements such as length, tone, and format. The complete prompt is submitted only after those elements are defined. Anthropic guidance likewise recommends clear instructions, relevant context, and explicit expected output.

**Learn more:** [Claude 4 Prompt Engineering Best Practices](https://docs.anthropic.com/zh-CN/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-4-best-practices)

definition.stemRaw: You are a bank manager who receives a request to use Claude as the sole decision-maker for customer credit-line approvals. Which response is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Accept the sole-decision-maker design because Claude can process applications faster than a human review team.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Expand the design so Claude both evaluates applications and issues final approval notices to customers directly.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Implement the design on a pilot basis and notify compliance only if issues arise during production use.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Decline the sole-decision-maker design and propose Claude assisting analysts who retain decision authority.

definition.explanation: Customer credit-line approvals are consequential financial decisions that require meaningful human oversight and accountable decision authority. Claude may assist analysts with evaluating applications, but analysts should retain the final approval authority.

definition.stemRaw:
A Claude associate is determining the bottleneck in a content workflow that is taking too long to publish. The workflow includes five steps: research, drafting, internal review, legal review, and publication. Cycle-time data is available for each step from the past month.  
  
Which signal most directly identifies the bottleneck?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the step where individual contributors report the highest workload based on their weekly status updates

choices.label: B
choices.text: the step most recently added to the workflow, based on the assumption that process changes introduce the most friction

choices.label: C
choices.text: the step with the longest queue or the largest backlog of items waiting to enter it

choices.label: D
choices.text: the step with the highest average cycle time per item across the past month’s runs

definition.explanation:
A bottleneck is the process step whose capacity constrains the throughput of the entire workflow. In a sequential workflow measured by cycle time, the step with the highest average cycle time is the slowest stage and most directly limits the rate at which items can progress and be published. Queue size may support that finding, but it is an indirect and potentially temporary symptom.

**Learn more:** [Cycle Time — Lean Enterprise Institute](https://www.lean.org/lexicon-terms/cycle-time/) · [What Is the Theory of Constraints, and How Does It Compare to Lean Thinking? — Lean Enterprise Institute](https://www.lean.org/the-lean-post/articles/what-is-the-theory-of-constraints-and-how-does-it-compare-to-lean-thinking/)

definition.stemRaw: You are setting up a new Claude Project for a particular recurring workload. Which Project-configuration step should be completed first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Define the purpose of the Project and the recurring tasks it must support.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Invite collaborators to the Project and confirm the appropriate access levels.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add reference materials and instructions that the Project will rely on.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Test the configured Project on a representative request from the workload.

definition.explanation:
A Project’s purpose and the recurring tasks it will support establish the context for its configuration. Reference materials, project instructions, collaborator permissions, and representative testing should be chosen and assessed against that defined workload.

**Learn more:** [What are projects?](https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/9517075-what-are-projects) · [How can I create and manage projects?](https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/9519177-how-can-i-create-and-manage-projects)

definition.stemRaw:
You are a business analyst assessing prompt drafts prepared by teammates.  
  
Which two components should be included in a well-structured prompt for a business task? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer represents part of the solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: a friendly, conversational tone instruction to make responses feel more approachable

choices.label: B
choices.text: a comprehensive list of company products and services to provide the model with business context

choices.label: C
choices.text: a short personal anecdote to make the prompt feel more conversational

choices.label: D
choices.text: a clear statement of the task that the model must perform

choices.label: E
choices.text: relevant context such as the audience and the goal of the task

definition.explanation: Effective business prompts specify the task the model is expected to perform and provide relevant context—such as the intended audience and the task goal—so the response can be targeted, appropriate, and useful.

definition.stemRaw:
A project lead is assessing a Claude-generated status report against the project charter. The report will be presented to a steering committee that expects an accurate status update against committed milestones.  
  
Which group of criteria offers the strongest evaluation framework?

choices.label: A
choices.text: length, formatting consistency, and tone appropriateness for a steering committee audience

choices.label: B
choices.text: accuracy of facts against the charter, completeness against required reporting fields, and relevance to the audience receiving the report

choices.label: C
choices.text: readability, narrative flow, and whether the report tells a coherent story about the project’s progress

choices.label: D
choices.text: match to the prior status report’s structure, since the steering committee expects consistent reporting from period to period

definition.explanation: A strong evaluation framework for a project status report verifies factual accuracy against the charter, confirms that all required reporting fields are complete, and assesses whether the content is relevant to the steering committee audience. These criteria directly support dependable reporting on committed milestones; presentation quality and structural consistency alone do not.

definition.stemRaw: A senior manager is reviewing a colleague’s practice of never updating their team’s Project configurations because “if it works once, it works forever.” Which feedback is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Configurations should be updated on a fixed schedule regardless of whether the underlying policies and source documents have changed, since regular maintenance prevents drift.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configurations should be updated only when output quality visibly degrades, since proactive updates risk introducing regressions in working configurations.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configurations should be reviewed and updated periodically because policies, terminology, and source documents change over time, even when output quality has not visibly degraded.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configurations should be left alone if the team is satisfied with current outputs, and any required updates should be handled at the chat level rather than the Project level.

definition.explanation: Project configurations should be reviewed and updated periodically because the policies, terminology, and source documents they rely on can change even before any decline in output quality is apparent.

definition.stemRaw:
You are organizing connected data sources for a team and must finish the planning steps before authorizing a connection. Which two planning steps must be completed **BEFORE** authorizing a new Connector? *(Choose two.)*  
  
Each correct answer represents part of the solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Migrate every existing report off the prior data source onto the new Connector.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Confirm the Connector is on the approved-vendor list maintained by IT.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Confirm the data classification of the source and the team’s permission to use it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Train every team member on the new Connector through formal training sessions.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Decommission any unused legacy connectors that may still be authorized.

definition.explanation: Authorizing a connector requires governance validation: the connector must be approved by IT, and the data source’s classification and the team’s permission to use it must be confirmed. These checks establish vendor and data-access compliance before a connection is authorized.

definition.stemRaw:
While preparing a stakeholder communication about a proposed Claude use case, a senior manager is applying the AI Fluency Framework **Description** competency.  
  
Which framing most closely reflects Description principles for stakeholder communication?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Describe what Claude can reliably produce for the use case, the known limitations, and the human oversight that will remain in place, calibrated to the audience’s familiarity with AI.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Overstate Claude’s capabilities to secure stakeholder support, even though Description principles require accurate framing of what Claude can and cannot reliably produce for the proposed use case.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Omit the human oversight that will remain in place from the communication, even though Description principles require setting expectations that reflect the actual capability boundaries of the use case.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Understate Claude’s capabilities to lower stakeholder expectations, even though Description principles require accuracy in both directions rather than systematic minimization of what Claude can produce.

definition.explanation:
Effective Description uses clear, purposeful communication to convey intended AI outputs and behavior. Accurate stakeholder framing should communicate what Claude can reliably produce, its known capability boundaries, and the human oversight that remains, in terms appropriate to the audience’s AI familiarity.

**Learn more:** [AI Fluency: Description](https://www.anthropic.com/ai-fluency/description) · [The AI Fluency Framework](https://www.anthropic.com/ai-fluency/overview)

definition.stemRaw:
You are a Claude associate conducting an ethics review of a Claude-assisted deliverable before it is published. What is the correct sequence of review steps?  
  
1. Confirm that transparency requirements are satisfied for the audience that will receive the deliverable.  
2. Record the review result and any modifications made.  
3. Identify the audience and the deliverable’s potential impact on that audience.  
4. Make focused revisions, or escalate when a concern needs greater authority to resolve.  
5. Review the content for unsupported generalizations, fairness concerns, and accuracy issues.
definition.explanation: An ethics review should establish who may be affected and how, assess the content for fairness and accuracy problems, determine the transparency required for that audience, address or escalate identified concerns, and retain a record of the final outcome and changes.

definition.stemRaw:
You are a business analyst assessing a Claude-generated business case against the agreed acceptance criteria. What is the correct sequence of evaluation steps?  
  
1. Compare the business case against the source data and required topics.  
2. Record gaps and inaccuracies for follow-up or correction.  
3. Reconfirm the acceptance criteria for the business case.  
4. Determine whether to use the business case, iterate, or escalate.  
5. Read the business case from start to finish to form an initial impression.
definition.explanation: A sound evaluation establishes the acceptance criteria before review, reads the complete business case for context, validates it against source data and required content, records deficiencies, and only then decides whether it is acceptable, needs iteration, or should be escalated.

definition.stemRaw:
A project manager is turning a Claude-generated draft into a polished board memo. The board reviews the memo before the meeting and expects it to be scannable, factually verified, and consistent with the organization’s standard terminology.  
  
Which set of refinements is most suitable?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apply consistent headings, tighten wording for executive scanability, align terminology with the organization’s standards, and verify each fact against source data.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Apply consistent headings, expand each section to give the board full context, and align terminology with the organization's standards.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tighten wording for executive scanability and verify each fact against source data; leave heading structure and terminology as written to preserve the draft’s voice.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Apply consistent headings and align terminology with the organization’s standards; rely on Claude’s verification of facts, since the draft was generated from the source data.

definition.explanation: A board memo should use consistent headings and concise wording for quick executive review, follow the organization’s standard terminology, and have every factual claim verified against source data. AI-generated content does not remove the need for independent fact checking.

definition.stemRaw:
You are an operations lead assessing prompting strategies proposed by teammates for different task types.  
  
Which two strategies are suitable matches between the strategy and task type? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer provides part of the solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: rigid templated prompting for early-stage creative naming and tagline ideation

choices.label: B
choices.text: open exploratory prompting for legal contract redlining against a clause library

choices.label: C
choices.text: open exploratory prompting for early-stage strategic brainstorming on a new market

choices.label: D
choices.text: rigid templated prompting for casual customer-feedback summarization with no schema

choices.label: E
choices.text: rigid templated prompting for monthly compliance reports against a fixed schema

definition.explanation: Open exploratory prompting supports divergent thinking during early-stage strategic brainstorming for a new market. Rigid templated prompting supports repeatable monthly compliance reports that must conform to a fixed schema.

definition.stemRaw:
A learning specialist is setting up a Claude Project for a recurring course-design workflow.  
  
Which configuration approach makes the best use of a Skill together with other Project elements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Configure the Project with custom instructions that contradict the Skill’s documented purpose, creating ambiguity about which guidance Claude should follow within the recurring course-design workflow.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add the relevant Skill to the Project, upload the supporting knowledge sources, and write custom instructions that reference both the Skill and the knowledge.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Upload the supporting knowledge sources but disable the relevant Skill, eliminating the packaged capability the workflow needs and forcing each chat to reconstruct the procedure manually.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add the Skill to the Project but omit the supporting knowledge sources and any custom instructions, so the Project lacks the reference content and persistent guidance the workflow requires.

definition.explanation:
Skills provide specialized, repeatable procedures, while a Project’s knowledge base provides persistent reference context and its project instructions provide guidance for chats in that Project. Adding the relevant Skill, supporting knowledge sources, and aligned custom instructions combines those complementary capabilities for a recurring workflow.

**Learn more:** [What are skills? | Anthropic Help Center](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512176-what-are-skills) · [How can I create and manage projects? | Anthropic Help Center](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9519177-how-can-i-create-and-manage-projects)

definition.stemRaw:
An operations assistant is using Claude to help optimize an existing intake workflow. The assistant can access the current process documentation and recent cycle-time data.  
  
Which activity makes the best use of Claude to support this process-optimization task?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Generate an optimized version of the intake process based on industry benchmarks, then compare it to the current process to identify gaps.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Apply Claude to predict the cycle-time impact of each proposed change and rank them so the team can implement improvements in priority order.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Map the current intake process, identify likely bottlenecks based on the cycle-time data, and propose optimization options for human review.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use Claude to interview each team member who works on the intake process and synthesize the interview output into a redesigned workflow.

definition.explanation:
Claude can analyze provided documentation and cycle-time data to map the current workflow, surface likely bottlenecks, and suggest optimization alternatives. Human review remains necessary because language-model outputs should be grounded in supplied evidence and validated before operational decisions are made.

**Learn more:** [Intro to Claude](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/welcome) · [Reduce hallucinations](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-hallucinations)

definition.stemRaw:
An associate is responding to an executive who asserts that Claude will remove the need for any human review of customer-facing content. The executive approves the team’s AI-tools budget.  
  
Which response is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Escalate the executive’s claim to a senior leader outside the team before responding directly, since the issue affects more than just the associate’s team.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pilot the executive’s proposal on a low-risk subset of customer-facing content first, and use the pilot results to make the case for retaining human review on higher-risk content.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Defer to the executive’s authority and remove the human review step from customer-facing content, monitoring the results closely for the first several weeks.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Acknowledge the productivity gains, then explain that human review remains essential on customer-facing content because of accuracy and brand risk, with specific examples.

definition.explanation:
Generative-model output can still contain factual errors, violate organizational policies, or fail to meet brand standards. Human review remains an important control for customer-facing material, particularly where accuracy and reputation matter; acknowledging efficiency gains while explaining those risks with concrete examples is the appropriate stakeholder response. Anthropic’s customer-support guidance recommends guardrails, fact-checking, and verification that agent responses align with company policies and known facts.

**Learn more:** [Anthropic Claude Platform Docs — Customer support agent](https://docs.anthropic.com/de/docs/about-claude/use-case-guides/customer-support-chat)

definition.stemRaw:
A support representative is setting up a Project to draft customer-facing apology emails following service outages. The current custom instructions tell Claude to “be empathetic and casual, keep it short, and offer a goodwill credit.” The customer-service team has reported that recent drafts are too brief, offer goodwill credits when policy does not permit them, and use contractions prohibited by the brand voice guide.  
  
Which change best aligns the configuration with the use case?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Replace “be empathetic and casual” with “match the brand voice guide,” remove the instruction to offer goodwill credits, and let each draft determine its own length based on the incident.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Move the brand voice guide and the goodwill-credit policy into the Project knowledge base and rely on the documents alone to govern tone, length, and credit decisions, without changing the custom instructions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Specify the brand voice attributes (empathetic, formal, no contractions), set a minimum length, and instruct Claude to recommend a goodwill credit only when the attached eligibility policy permits one.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Keep the existing instructions and add a sentence telling Claude to consult the brand voice guide and the goodwill-credit policy that are attached to the Project knowledge base.

definition.explanation: Custom instructions should state the required voice attributes and operational constraints explicitly: empathetic but formal language with no contractions, a minimum draft length, and goodwill-credit recommendations only when the attached eligibility policy authorizes them. This prevents the overly brief, casual, and policy-inconsistent outputs.

definition.stemRaw:
You are an HR specialist assessing model selections made by colleagues for different tasks. Which two model choices are appropriate matches between the model and the task? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer provides a complete solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: a higher-capability model selected solely because it is the most expensive option

choices.label: B
choices.text: a higher-capability model for one-line keyword extraction at high request volume

choices.label: C
choices.text: a higher-capability model for complex multi-step legal reasoning under review

choices.label: D
choices.text: a lighter, faster model for nuanced multi-document strategic synthesis

choices.label: E
choices.text: a lighter, faster model for routine FAQ-style replies under tight latency budgets

definition.explanation:
Higher-capability models are appropriate for complex, multi-step reasoning tasks such as legal analysis, where stronger reasoning quality is needed and human review can validate the result. Lighter, faster models are appropriate for routine, well-defined FAQ responses when low latency is a priority. Model selection should be based on task complexity, quality needs, cost, and latency—not price alone.

**Learn more:** [Models | OpenAI API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/models)

definition.stemRaw:
You are a project manager at Orinexa, Inc. You are selecting a Claude model for a new production workload and must finish the requirements steps before testing candidates.  
  
Which two steps must be completed **BEFORE** testing candidate models on a representative sample? *(Choose two.)*  
  
Each correct answer represents part of the solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Define the quality bar, the latency tolerance, and the expected request volume.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Retest the selected model whenever a new model version is released.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Choose a candidate model based on the requirements profile and known capabilities.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Promote the selected model to production traffic for the workload.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sign off on the production rollout plan with the platform and security teams.

definition.explanation:
A production model evaluation needs measurable success criteria and operational constraints—including quality, latency, and expected request volume—so results can be judged against the workload’s requirements. Candidate models must also be shortlisted according to that requirements profile and their known capabilities before they are evaluated on representative traffic. Anthropic guidance calls for defining measurable success criteria before building evaluations, and AWS guidance describes benchmarking candidate models against a workload-specific evaluation set after determining the required quality and latency characteristics.

**Learn more:** [Define success criteria and build evaluations — Claude Platform Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/develop-tests) · [Implement task-appropriate model selection strategies — AWS Well-Architected Agentic AI Lens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/agentic-ai-lens/agentperf02-bp02.html)

definition.stemRaw:
You are a communications specialist who is preparing to explain Claude’s role in a workflow to several stakeholder groups and must finish the preparation activities before drafting messages.  
  
Which two preparation activities must be completed **BEFORE** drafting the stakeholder messages? *(Choose two.)*  
  
Each correct answer represents part of the solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Archive the drafted messages in the corporate communications repository.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Identify the stakeholder groups and what each group needs to understand

choices.label: C
choices.text: Define the key facts about Claude’s role and the boundaries that apply.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Send the drafted messages out and gather feedback for revision.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Schedule a follow-up forum to handle questions raised by the messages.

definition.explanation: Effective stakeholder messaging requires identifying each stakeholder group and what it needs to understand, along with defining the key facts about Claude’s role and the boundaries that apply. These inputs establish the message content and audience framing before drafting begins.

definition.stemRaw:
You are an operations manager creating a quick-reference card for a team.  
  
Which description accurately characterizes the three Claude model tiers in general terms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Haiku is the most capable model for the deepest reasoning, while Opus is the lightweight model for quick replies.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All three models offer the same reasoning depth and differ only in response speed and cost.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Haiku is fast and lightweight, Sonnet is the balanced default for most everyday work, and Opus is the most capable for complex reasoning at higher latency and cost.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sonnet is the fastest of the three models because its architecture is optimized for speed rather than reasoning depth.

definition.explanation:
Claude Haiku is the lightweight, fast, lower-cost tier; Claude Sonnet balances capability, efficiency, and cost for general work; and Claude Opus is the highest-capability tier for demanding, complex reasoning, with higher cost and typically greater latency.

**Learn more:** [Intro to Claude](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/welcome) · [Anthropic pricing](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/about-claude/pricing)

definition.stemRaw:
You are a project manager having an extended planning conversation with Claude and need to keep it productive as it expands. Which two practices help keep a long planning conversation productive? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer provides a complete solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Open a new thread for every minor follow-up question to keep threads short.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Restate constraints and goals when the focus shifts to a new subtopic.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Periodically summarize decisions made so far to compress the working state.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Switch context aggressively between unrelated planning topics within one thread

choices.label: E
choices.text: Avoid summarizing so the model retains every original word it has produced.

definition.explanation:
Reasserting goals and constraints when the discussion moves to a new subtopic maintains alignment with the project’s requirements. Periodically summarizing decisions preserves the important working state in a compact form, helping the model maintain coherence as the conversation approaches context-window limits.

**Learn more:** [Anthropic Claude Platform Docs: Glossary — Context window](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/glossary)

definition.stemRaw: A finance manager is preparing to discuss a confidential pre-announcement figure with Claude. Which two settings most closely follow sound privacy practices for this discussion? (Choose two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Skip the privacy setting decision and proceed with default behavior, since the conversation will not explicitly instruct Claude to remember the figure.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Disable Memory contribution for the conversation if Incognito mode is not used, so the confidential figure is not retained as persistent context that could surface in later unrelated sessions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Treat the conversation as appropriate for default Memory settings, since the figure will only be discussed briefly and is unlikely to be retained.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enable Memory contribution for the conversation so the context carries forward to support follow-up analysis in future sessions.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Open the conversation in Incognito mode, which prevents the conversation from contributing to Memory and avoids persistent retention of the confidential pre-announcement figure across sessions.

definition.explanation:
Confidential financial information should not be allowed to become persistent context that could be surfaced in later, unrelated sessions. Disable the conversation’s Memory contribution when using a standard conversation, or use Incognito mode to prevent the conversation from contributing to Memory. Anthropic also advises care when sharing highly sensitive financial information and confidential business documents.

**Learn more:** [Anthropic Help Center: Sensitive data in Claude conversations](https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/8325621-i-would-like-to-input-sensitive-data-into-my-free-pro-or-max-plan-claude-account-who-can-view-my-conversations)

definition.stemRaw:
A knowledge worker is explaining how feedback can be used to improve Claude-supported work over time.  
  
Which description is the most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Capture specific feedback after each run, translate it into targeted prompt or workflow changes, and observe whether subsequent runs improve.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Capture feedback only after several runs so patterns emerge from the volume of observations, then apply changes based on the patterns rather than any single run.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Capture feedback as an aggregate quality score per run, since aggregate scores show whether quality is improving without requiring detail on individual issues.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Capture general impressions after each run and apply them as broad prompt rewrites, since broad rewrites cover more potential issues than targeted changes.

definition.explanation: An effective improvement loop captures specific feedback after each run, maps it to targeted prompt or workflow adjustments, and checks later runs for measurable improvement. Specific, timely feedback makes the cause of a change and its effect on output quality easier to evaluate.

definition.stemRaw:
You are a Claude associate investigating a recurring instance of poor output.  
  
Which diagnostic-step sequence is correct?  
  
1. Develop a hypothesis about the prompt element most likely responsible for the deficiency.  
2. Make one targeted change and observe its effect on the output.  
3. Read the output from beginning to end and identify the specific deficiency.  
4. Compare the deficient output with the prompt to find mismatches between the input and output.  
5. Record the root cause and resolution for future reference.
definition.explanation: Effective prompt-output troubleshooting first identifies the precise output defect and compares it with the prompt to establish the relevant mismatch. The resulting evidence supports a causal hypothesis, which should be tested by changing only one targeted element. Documenting the confirmed cause and resolution preserves the result for later reuse.

definition.stemRaw: You have revised a Claude prompt eight times, and output quality has plateaued during the last four attempts. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Iteration should stop and the current output should be accepted as-is regardless of remaining issues.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Iteration should stop and the task should be abandoned without communicating to stakeholders.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Iteration has reached diminishing returns and the next step is human review or a different approach.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Iteration should continue indefinitely because more attempts always improve quality.

definition.explanation: When several successive prompt iterations no longer improve output quality, further revisions are producing diminishing returns. Human review or a different approach is the appropriate next step.

definition.stemRaw: You are a project manager assessing workflow steps by the amount of leverage Claude integration provides. Which workflow step generally delivers the greatest Claude leverage for a knowledge-work team?

choices.label: A
choices.text: approving final deliverables for external publication without further review

choices.label: B
choices.text: negotiating contractual terms with external parties on behalf of the company

choices.label: C
choices.text: drafting and synthesizing across many sources for a downstream reviewer

choices.label: D
choices.text: making final personnel decisions about hiring, promotion, or termination

definition.explanation: Claude is most useful for drafting and synthesizing information from many sources, where it can accelerate preparation of material while a downstream reviewer retains responsibility for validation and final judgment.

definition.stemRaw:
You are conducting a weekly feedback-and-adjustment cycle.  
  
What is the correct sequence of cycle steps?  
  
1. Turn feedback into one or two focused adjustments for the next cycle.  
2. Run the following cycle and compare its results with the previous cycle.  
3. Record the specific feedback received during the review.  
4. Document what changed, the effect it created, and any unresolved issues.  
5. Determine whether to keep iterating, change approaches, or escalate.
definition.explanation: A closed feedback loop records the review feedback before selecting targeted adjustments. The adjusted cycle is then run and measured against the prior cycle; its changes and outcomes are documented so there is a basis for deciding whether to iterate further, change direction, or escalate.

definition.stemRaw: You are a content creator. Claude’s initial response is accurate but uses inconsistent terminology that does not align with your organization’s glossary. Which iterative revision addresses this issue most directly?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase the requested length so the inconsistent terminology appears more often.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ask Claude to invent additional terms unrelated to the glossary.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Remove the topic from the prompt to avoid the terminology issue entirely.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Provide the organization's glossary and instruct Claude to use only those terms throughout the response.

definition.explanation: Providing the organization’s glossary and requiring exclusive use of its terms gives Claude the approved vocabulary and a clear constraint to apply it consistently throughout the response.

definition.stemRaw:
You are a knowledge manager organizing source material within the context window for a lengthy Claude evaluation task.  
  
Which two practices result in more effective use of the context window? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer provides a complete solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Paste every available document into context regardless of relevance to the task.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mark each source clearly with delimiters so the model can attribute claims correctly.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Repeat the same instruction at the start, middle, and end to reinforce it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mix sources together in a single block so the model can synthesize them freely.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Place the most reference-critical material near the beginning or end of context.

definition.explanation:
Clear, descriptive delimiters such as XML tags separate documents, metadata, instructions, and inputs, reducing ambiguity and supporting correct source attribution. For long-context work, placing long-form reference material near the top and the task query near the end improves performance; therefore, reference-critical content should be positioned near a context boundary rather than buried in the middle.

**Learn more:** [Anthropic Claude prompting best practices](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices)

definition.stemRaw:
A knowledge worker regularly switches between Claude and another AI service while working on a long-running project.  
  
Which Claude feature most directly minimizes repetitive context-setting across sessions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enable Memory and use the import capability to bring relevant context from the other AI service into Claude as a starting point for the project’s work.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Rely on a single static Artifact pasted into each chat as the only continuity mechanism, ignoring the Memory feature that is purpose-built for retaining work-relevant context across sessions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Open every Claude session in Incognito mode, which prevents the conversation from contributing to Memory and therefore eliminates the cross-session continuity the project would benefit from.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Disable Memory entirely and re-paste the same context paragraphs at the start of every Claude session, even though Memory is designed to retain that context across conversations automatically.

definition.explanation:
Claude Memory retains work-related context for use in new conversations, and its built-in import flow can bring relevant memory from another AI service into Claude. This reduces the need to repeatedly provide the same project context across sessions.

**Learn more:** [Import and export your memory from Claude](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12123587-import-and-export-your-memory-from-claude) · [Use Claude’s chat search and memory to build on previous context](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11817273-use-claude-s-chat-search-and-memory-to-build-on-previous-context)

definition.stemRaw:
An HR business partner is setting up a new Project for recurring policy questions from managers. The Project will be used across many chats by several HR team members.  
  
Which content should belong in the Project knowledge base?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the current employee handbook plus prior versions of the handbook going back five years, so Claude can answer questions about how policies have changed

choices.label: B
choices.text: the current employee handbook, the leveling guide, the policies-FAQ, and every email the HR team has sent about policy in the past year, for additional context

choices.label: C
choices.text: the current employee handbook only, with the leveling guide and the policies-FAQ attached at the start of each chat as needed for that chat’s topic

choices.label: D
choices.text: the current employee handbook, the leveling guide, and the policies-FAQ document referenced across the Project’s chats

definition.explanation:
A Project knowledge base supplies context across all chats in that Project, so it should contain the current, broadly relevant reference documents needed repeatedly for manager policy questions: the current employee handbook, leveling guide, and policies FAQ. Superseded policies and incidental historical emails can introduce outdated or unnecessary context, while recurring reference materials should not need to be attached separately to each chat.

**Learn more:** [How can I create and manage projects?](https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/9519177-how-can-i-create-and-manage-projects) · [Usage Limit Best Practices](https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices)

definition.stemRaw:
A knowledge worker is briefing a stakeholder group about Claude’s limitations. The stakeholders will use Claude for customer-facing work, where confident-sounding output containing errors could cause real harm.  
  
Which limitation is most important to communicate clearly?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Claude’s responses vary across runs of the same prompt, so stakeholders should run each prompt several times and compare outputs before using any single response.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Claude can produce confident-sounding output that contains unsupported claims, so human review remains essential for high-impact work.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Claude can produce long, detailed responses that take time to read, so stakeholders should request shorter outputs when working under tight deadlines.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Claude’s knowledge has a training cutoff, so stakeholders must verify any time-sensitive claims against current sources before using them.

definition.explanation:
Claude can sometimes hallucinate, producing text that is factually incorrect or inconsistent with the provided context despite sounding plausible or confident. Hallucination-mitigation measures cannot eliminate this risk, so critical information and high-impact customer-facing output require human review and verification.

**Learn more:** [Reduce hallucinations - Claude Platform Docs](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-hallucinations)

definition.stemRaw:
You are a knowledge worker preparing material for a Claude prompt.  
  
Which data type most clearly needs additional handling, such as redaction or anonymization, before it is included in the prompt?

choices.label: A
choices.text: public press releases the company has already published

choices.label: B
choices.text: customer government identifiers and full payment-card numbers tied to named individuals

choices.label: C
choices.text: job titles taken from the company’s public organizational chart

choices.label: D
choices.text: generic product descriptions available on the company’s marketing site

definition.explanation:
Government identifiers and full payment-card numbers associated with identifiable people are sensitive personal and financial data. Redacting or anonymizing them reduces unnecessary exposure of personally identifiable information; public company materials and generic public product information do not create the same privacy risk.

**Learn more:** [Customer support agent — Claude Platform Docs](https://docs.anthropic.com/de/docs/about-claude/use-case-guides/customer-support-chat)

definition.stemRaw:
You are an operations lead who is integrating Claude into a workflow used by multiple people.  
  
Which integration step should be completed first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Identify where Claude adds value and where each handoff to a human occurs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pilot the integrated workflow with a small group on representative work.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Iterate the integrated workflow based on the findings from the pilot.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Document the integrated workflow and onboard the rest of the team to it.

definition.explanation:
A human–AI workflow must first define the tasks where Claude provides value and the points at which responsibility passes to a human. Those boundaries establish the workflow that can later be piloted, refined from pilot results, documented, and rolled out. Anthropic guidance likewise emphasizes keeping humans in the loop and defining organizational gates around agentic work.

**Learn more:** [The AI-Native SDLC playbook](https://claude.com/blog/the-ai-native-sdlc-playbook?categoryid=2826672%3Fcategoryid%3D2826672&fcdaa149_sort_date=desc)

definition.stemRaw:
A Claude associate is assessing a proposed use case in which Claude would make final hiring decisions without any human review, using the AI Fluency Framework’s Delegation competency.  
  
Which classification most accurately reflects Delegation principles?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inappropriate for full AI delegation, because hiring decisions involve human judgment, accountability, and consequences that Delegation criteria reserve for human ownership rather than autonomous AI execution.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Appropriate with light human review applied only to a sample of decisions, even though Delegation criteria reserve final hiring decisions for human ownership rather than sample-based oversight after the fact.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Appropriate for full AI delegation, on the basis that processing speed outweighs the human judgment, accountability, and consequence considerations that Delegation criteria require for final hiring decisions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inappropriate only because of system reliability concerns rather than accountability, even though Delegation criteria classify final hiring decisions as requiring human ownership regardless of system performance.

definition.explanation:
Delegation involves strategically distributing work between people and AI based on the task’s nature, the system’s capabilities and limitations, and the need for human expertise and judgment. Final hiring decisions carry consequential human judgment and accountability, so they require human ownership rather than autonomous AI execution.

**Learn more:** [AI Fluency: Delegation](https://www.anthropic.com/ai-fluency/ai-fluency-delegation?adid=online&campaignid=ms_search_a&campaignname=eur-ieen_ms-competitorsgen-edp-online_mt-exact&device=m&f0=typesfaculty&field_format_value=2&internal_source=intheknow&mode=list_insead_stories&programme_code=ltf&search_api_fulltext=&siteid=ms&term=londonschoolofeconomicsonlinecourses_e)

definition.stemRaw: You are assessing a Claude output that seems to include hallucinated content. Which response step should be taken first when a hallucination is suspected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Discard the entire output and regenerate the output with a fresh prompt.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Document the hallucination pattern in the team’s risk register for future reference.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Notify the user community that the output contains a hallucinated claim.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pinpoint the specific claim that appears to be unsupported by available evidence.

definition.explanation:
A hallucination is an assertion that lacks factual support or conflicts with reliable evidence. Identifying the exact unsupported claim establishes what must be verified, corrected, withdrawn, or escalated; regeneration, risk documentation, and user notification are subsequent actions. Anthropic recommends verifying claims with supporting quotations and sources, and withdrawing a claim when no supporting citation can be found.

**Learn more:** [Reduce hallucinations - Claude Platform Docs](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-hallucinations)

definition.stemRaw:
You are optimizing a recurring Claude workflow and must finish the diagnostic steps before modifying the workflow. Which two diagnostic steps must be completed **BEFORE** changing the recurring workflow? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer represents part of the solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Notify executive leadership of the projected savings from the optimization.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Identify the steps that contribute most to time, cost, or quality issues.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deploy the updated workflow across the team and monitor for adoption issues.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Measure the current workflow's quality, time, and cost across recent runs.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Document the revised workflow steps and update the team’s standard operating procedures.

definition.explanation: Workflow optimization requires a baseline measurement of current quality, time, and cost, plus identification of the steps creating the greatest time, cost, or quality issues. Those diagnostics establish what to change and provide a basis for evaluating whether the revised workflow improves outcomes.

definition.stemRaw: Before sharing a Claude-generated brief, an analyst applies the AI Fluency Framework’s Discernment competency to assess it. Which review most accurately reflects Discernment principles?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Accept the brief on the basis that it reads fluently and the subject matter aligns with the analyst’s professional knowledge of the topic.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Skip the source material check during review and rely on overall tone and logical flow as proxies for factual accuracy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Review the opening paragraph and the conclusion of the brief, since these sections typically reflect the quality of the full document.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Conduct a systematic check of the brief against the task requirements, source material, and professional standards before sharing it.

definition.explanation:
Discernment involves thoughtfully and critically evaluating AI outputs for quality, including accuracy, relevance, coherence, and appropriateness. Checking the complete brief against its requirements, underlying sources, and professional standards provides the evidence needed before it is shared.

**Learn more:** [AI Fluency: Discernment](https://www.anthropic.com/ai-fluency/discernment)

definition.stemRaw:
You are using Claude to redesign an employee onboarding workflow and must finish the high-level decomposition steps before defining detailed artifacts.  
  
Which two decomposition steps must be completed **before** specifying the exact email content and schedule? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer represents part of the solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pilot the onboarding workflow with a small cohort of new hires.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Identify the major phases of the onboarding experience.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Negotiate the onboarding budget with the finance department.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Define the overall objective of the onboarding experience.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Roll out the onboarding workflow to every new hire across the company.

definition.explanation: A sound high-level decomposition begins by defining the onboarding experience’s overall objective and identifying its major phases. Those decisions establish the structure and purpose that detailed artifacts, such as exact email copy and scheduling, must follow.

definition.stemRaw: You are refining a prompt across several iterations. With every change, the output drifts farther from the requested template. Which step is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Discard all prior versions and start with no record of what worked.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Continue making large simultaneous changes until the output happens to align.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Revert to the version of the prompt that produced the closest match and adjust from that baseline.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stop iterating and accept the most off-target version.

definition.explanation: Prompt refinement is most effective when it resumes from the version that most closely met the required template. That baseline preserves the successful elements and enables small, controlled adjustments instead of compounding drift.

definition.stemRaw:
You are assessing items proposed for inclusion in a Project that supports policy summaries.  
  
Which two items are suitable to include in the Project? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer represents part of the solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: the summary format and the audience expectations the summaries must meet

choices.label: B
choices.text: the current policy library that the summaries are drawn from

choices.label: C
choices.text: presentation slides from a recent team training session on internal communication standards

choices.label: D
choices.text: active client case files maintained by a separate legal team for a different workstream

choices.label: E
choices.text: employee onboarding records used in a separate HR workflow managed by the same team

definition.explanation:
Project instructions can define how ChatGPT should respond, including required format and audience expectations. A Project can also contain reference materials that ChatGPT uses to produce informed results, so the current policy library belongs in the policy-summary workflow. Unrelated training, legal-case, and HR-onboarding materials are outside that workflow and should not be added as its context.

**Learn more:** [Projects in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-using-projects-in-chatgpt)

definition.stemRaw: You are categorizing structural defects in Claude output by how much they undermine clarity. Which structural defect most seriously impairs the output’s clarity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A single subheading is shorter than the other subheadings in the document.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Two adjacent paragraphs present the same information using inconsistent terminology.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Typographic inconsistencies appear throughout multiple sections of the document.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The main conclusion contradicts the evidence presented in the body.
