definition.explanation: A main conclusion that conflicts with the evidence in the body creates a fundamental logical inconsistency. It leaves the reader unable to determine which claim is supported, undermining the clarity and reliability of the output’s central message.

definition.stemRaw:
As a communications manager, you are validating a Claude-generated newsletter that contains a specific industry-growth figure. The figure is reported in three trade-press articles, but none links to the underlying study.  
  
Which validation step is appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Accept the figure because three trade-press articles repeat it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Remove the source attribution and present the figure as common knowledge.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Locate the original study referenced by the trade-press articles and verify the figure in the primary source.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use the highest figure across the three articles to make the newsletter more compelling.

definition.explanation: A figure repeated across secondary trade-press articles can originate from the same unverified claim. Validating it requires locating the underlying study and confirming the figure, its methodology, scope, and context in the primary source.

definition.stemRaw:
You are preparing a document with mixed-sensitivity content for use with Claude.  
  
Which data-handling action should be completed first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Redact sensitive fields and replace them with appropriate placeholders.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Classify the content of the document and identify which fields are sensitive.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Submit the redacted document to Claude for the intended task.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Review the redacted document with a peer to confirm the redaction is complete.

definition.explanation:
Sensitive fields must be identified through content classification before they can be safely redacted or replaced. This also supports the least-privilege principle: Claude should not receive sensitive information that it does not need.

**Learn more:** [Mitigate jailbreaks — Claude Platform Docs](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/mitigate-jailbreaks)

definition.stemRaw:
A finance consultant is revising a Claude-generated narrative for a quarterly investor update. Investors have a fixed time window for the call and expect the headline result and forward outlook to be made clear early.  
  
Which adaptation is most suitable for this audience?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lead with the quarter’s operational highlights, present the financial result in the middle for context, and close with the forward outlook.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lead with the forward outlook, since investors are most interested in what comes next, and present the headline result and drivers afterward.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lead with the headline result, present the key drivers concisely, and close with the forward outlook.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lead with a chronological recap of the quarter’s events, present the headline result at the natural end of the recap, and conclude with the forward outlook.

definition.explanation: Quarterly investor communications should prioritize the headline financial result early, followed by a concise explanation of its key drivers and the forward outlook. This structure makes the most decision-relevant information clear within a limited time window.

definition.stemRaw:
A knowledge worker is describing the purpose of an organizational AI governance framework to a colleague.  
  
Which description is the most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A governance framework defines approved tools, allowed data, required reviews, and reporting paths so AI is used consistently and accountably.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A governance framework lists the AI tools the organization licenses and the cost of each, so users can pick the most cost-effective tool for each task.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A governance framework defines the training every employee must complete before using AI tools, with separate requirements for each tool the organization licenses.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A governance framework documents the AI policies the organization is legally required to adopt, focusing on regulatory compliance rather than day-to-day use.

definition.explanation:
An AI governance framework sets organizational policies, processes, controls, roles, and accountability for AI throughout its use. It can define permitted tools and data, review requirements, and reporting or escalation paths so AI is used consistently, responsibly, and accountably. NIST identifies governance as establishing transparent policies, procedures, and controls, with documented roles and communication lines for AI risk management.

**Learn more:** [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/nist.ai.100-1.pdf)

definition.stemRaw:
A senior project coordinator has been asked to use Claude to create an end-of-year report covering finance, operations, and customer outcomes. The three areas have distinct data owners and separate source documents.  
  
Which decomposition approach is most likely to result in a strong report?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Define the report goals, gather inputs per section, draft each section in its own prompt, then synthesize the executive summary from the drafted sections.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Draft the executive summary first to anchor the report's narrative, then draft each section so it supports the summary already written.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Draft the three sections in parallel, each using a section-specific prompt, then concatenate and lightly edit the outputs into the final report.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prompt Claude once with all source documents and request the full report, including the executive summary, in a single pass.

definition.explanation: A strong cross-functional report is developed by defining its goals, collecting the appropriate inputs for each section, drafting those sections with focused prompts, and deriving the executive summary from the completed sections. This supports traceability to each area’s source material and ensures that the summary reflects the report’s actual findings.

definition.stemRaw:
A customer-success associate is preparing a prompt asking Claude to summarize a customer issue from a case file. The case file contains the customer’s full government identifier, home address, name, account number, and a description of the issue. The associate needs a summary focused on the issue.  
  
Which approach is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Submit the full case file and include an instruction telling Claude not to reference the government identifier or the home address in the summary.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Replace the government identifier with the customer’s name and the home address with the account number, since names and account numbers are less sensitive than identifiers and addresses.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Remove or redact the government identifier and the home address before submitting the prompt, since neither is necessary for a summary of the issue.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Submit only the description of the issue and add the customer’s name for context, since the description plus a name is sufficient to produce a summary.

definition.explanation: Data minimization requires providing only the information needed for the intended task. Because the summary is about the issue, the government identifier and home address are unnecessary sensitive data and should be removed or redacted before submission.

definition.stemRaw:
You are a process consultant incorporating Claude into an existing weekly workflow. Which sequence of integration steps is correct?  
  
1. Pilot the integrated workflow with a small group and collect feedback.  
2. Document the current workflow’s steps, owners, and decision points.  
3. Update the documented workflow and deploy it to the broader team.  
4. Identify the steps where Claude can augment work and where humans must remain.  
5. Define the inputs Claude requires, the outputs Claude provides, and the hand-offs around each step.
definition.explanation:
Workflow integration should begin with documenting the current process so its ownership and decision points are understood. That enables appropriate allocation of Claude-assisted and human-controlled work, followed by a clear specification of inputs, outputs, and hand-offs. A limited pilot validates the integrated process and gathers feedback before the workflow is revised and rolled out broadly. Anthropic guidance similarly recommends breaking an interaction into tasks, defining success criteria, and evaluating it systematically before production deployment.

**Learn more:** [Customer Support Agent — Claude Platform Docs](https://docs.anthropic.com/de/docs/about-claude/use-case-guides/customer-support-chat)

definition.stemRaw:
A customer-success team member reviews a Claude-generated customer health-check report against the agreed deliverable list. The report addresses all five required topics, but its renewal-risk section identifies only one risk factor, whereas the deliverable specification requires renewal risk to be evaluated across pricing, product fit, and stakeholder change.  
  
Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The report’s completeness cannot be assessed from the deliverable specification alone; the customer should review the output and confirm whether the renewal-risk depth is sufficient.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The report does not meet the deliverable specification because a section that addresses only one of three required risk dimensions counts as a missing section.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The report meets the deliverable specification because all five required topics appear and the renewal-risk section is present in the output.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The report meets the topic-level requirements but the renewal-risk section is under-scoped against the specification and should be expanded before delivery.

definition.explanation: A deliverable can satisfy the presence of each required topic while still failing a topic-specific depth requirement. Renewal risk must cover pricing, product fit, and stakeholder change; addressing only one factor leaves that section under-scoped and requires expansion before delivery.

definition.stemRaw: An analyst has been asked to calculate summary statistics from an uploaded sales-data file and create a chart for a weekly report. Which output approach is the best fit for this task?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ask Claude to estimate the summary statistics from a brief preview of the file, accepting unverified figures rather than running the calculations against the full uploaded dataset.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Produce a written placeholder for the chart in the chat response without generating the actual visualization, leaving the weekly report without the visual output it requires.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Request a narrative description of the data in the chat response without computing values, leaving the summary statistics and the chart unproduced and the weekly report incomplete.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use Code Execution to perform the calculations and generate the chart, then verify the computed results against the source data before sharing the output.

definition.explanation: Code Execution can calculate statistics from the full uploaded dataset, create the required chart, and support verification of the computed outputs against the underlying source data before they are shared.

definition.stemRaw:
You are preparing system-level instructions for a Project that supports recurring writing tasks.  
  
Which action should be completed first when creating the system-level instructions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Refine the drafted instructions based on observed gaps from validation runs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Validate the drafted instructions against representative requests for the Project.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Define the purpose of the Project and the boundaries the instructions must respect.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Distribute the finalized instructions to collaborators on the Project.

definition.explanation:
Effective system-level instructions begin by establishing the Project’s purpose and the boundaries that govern its behavior. Those requirements determine what the instructions should direct; drafting, validation, refinement, and distribution can occur only after that foundation is defined. Project instructions provide project-specific guidance for how ChatGPT should help within the Project.

**Learn more:** [Projects in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-using-projects-in-chatgpt)

definition.stemRaw:
A business analyst is asked to use Claude to extract requirements from a recorded stakeholder-interview transcript. The transcript is about 90 minutes long and addresses multiple topics.  
  
Which approach is most likely to yield usable structured output?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Provide the transcript along with a structured prompt that requests must-haves, nice-to-haves, open questions, and conflicts as separate sections.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Provide the transcript and ask Claude to produce a single ranked list of requirements, since a single list is easier for stakeholders to review than separate sections.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Provide the transcript and ask Claude to summarize it; extract requirements from the summary in a second pass since two passes catch more detail.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Provide the transcript and ask Claude to produce a chronological list of every statement that contains a verb, then classify each statement as a requirement or not.

definition.explanation:
Explicitly requesting separate categories for mandatory requirements, optional requirements, unresolved questions, and conflicts gives the model a clear output structure and preserves distinctions needed for requirements analysis. Clear, specific formatting instructions improve control over Claude’s response format.

**Learn more:** [Claude 4 prompting best practices](https://docs.anthropic.com/zh-CN/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-4-best-practices)

definition.stemRaw:
You received an imprecise request to “look at our pricing.” After discovery, the objective is confirmed: create a structured competitor-pricing summary the team can act on, rather than develop new pricing ideas.  
  
Which strategy best suits the clarified task?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use a divergent brainstorming approach to generate a wide range of possible competitor-pricing observations, then narrow to the most likely ones.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use a comparative analysis strategy that contrasts the company’s pricing against a single named competitor, since pairwise comparison produces the clearest output.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use a research strategy that gathers structured information about competitor pricing, names sources, and notes confidence in each finding.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use an open conversational strategy that explores competitor pricing iteratively across several prompts, allowing the structure to emerge from the conversation.

definition.explanation: A structured competitor-pricing summary requires research that collects comparable pricing information, identifies the sources for each finding, and records confidence or uncertainty so the team can judge how actionable the information is. This is an evidence-gathering and synthesis task, not brainstorming, a restricted single-competitor comparison, or open-ended conversation.

definition.stemRaw: You are a customer-success manager deciding whether to escalate a Claude-generated response. Which factor most strongly increases the output’s impact and warrants escalation before it is used externally?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The response is an internal draft summarizing the associate’s notes from a customer call for their own reference.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The response is a casual rephrasing of an internal team status update.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The response is a brief internal announcement about an upcoming team all-hands meeting.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The response is an unchanged draft for a paying customer that includes a service-level commitment.

definition.explanation:
An unchanged customer-facing draft that makes a service-level commitment can create an external promise with contractual, operational, and financial consequences. Its direct effect on a paying customer makes human review and escalation appropriate before use. Anthropic advises review by a qualified professional before disseminating sensitive content or decisions to consumers.

**Learn more:** [Anthropic Help Center: Planning to launch a product using Claude](https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/8241216-i-m-planning-to-launch-a-product-using-claude-what-steps-should-i-take-to-ensure-i-m-not-violating-anthropic-s-usage-policy)

definition.stemRaw:
An HR associate is getting ready to use Claude for a sensitive personnel matter. The organization’s AI policy expressly says that information concerning ongoing investigations must not be entered into AI tools.  
  
Which response most closely follows the policy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enter the investigation-related information into Claude only after the investigation closes, since the policy applies during the investigation period.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Refrain from entering investigation-related information into Claude and consult HR leadership for an approved alternative way to handle the matter.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enter the investigation-related information into Claude in an Incognito chat, since Incognito chats do not retain information and therefore fall outside the policy’s intent.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enter a paraphrased version of the investigation-related information that removes identifying details, since paraphrasing addresses the spirit of the policy.

definition.explanation: Information connected to an ongoing investigation must not be entered into an AI tool under the organization’s explicit policy. The appropriate course is to withhold the information from Claude and consult HR leadership for an approved alternative process.

definition.stemRaw:
A knowledge worker is refining a prompt that has generated a partially acceptable response.  
  
Which refinement practice yields the strongest learning across iterations?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change one identifiable element per iteration, capture the change and its effect, and adjust another element only after the first is settled.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Restart from a fresh prompt each iteration so that prior wording does not bias the next attempt, and pick the strongest response at the end.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Make several related changes in one iteration when they target the same weakness, and revert the whole set if the combined change makes the output worse.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Address every weakness the response showed in a single revision, then compare the revised output against the prior version.

definition.explanation: Controlled prompt refinement changes one identifiable variable at a time and records the resulting effect. This isolates which change caused an improvement or regression, enabling reliable learning and deliberate subsequent adjustments.

definition.stemRaw:
You are assessing Connector configurations that colleagues have suggested for different tasks. Which two Connector configurations are safe and suitable uses? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer provides a complete solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: a Connector that links to the personnel-records system for team leads to support scheduling tasks

choices.label: B
choices.text: a Connector that links to the team's project management workspace under approved scope

choices.label: C
choices.text: a Connector that links to a personal cloud storage account where team member’s store working drafts alongside personal files

choices.label: D
choices.text: a read-only Connector that links to the public knowledge base for reference content

choices.label: E
choices.text: a Connector that links to the payroll system to allow team members to submit expense reports directly

definition.explanation:
Appropriate Connector use follows least privilege, approved role-scoped access, and read-only access where writing is unnecessary. A Connector limited to an approved team project-management workspace and a read-only Connector to public reference content meet those constraints. Personnel, personal mixed-use storage, and payroll systems expose sensitive data or high-impact capabilities beyond the stated needs.

**Learn more:** [Admin Controls, Security, and Compliance in Apps](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11509118) · [Apps in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11487775-connectors-in-chatgpt)

definition.stemRaw:
A communications manager is preparing a prompt for Claude to create a quarterly newsletter for store managers across three regions. The agreed key messages, regional information, and a previous newsletter the team liked are all available.  
  
Which prompt strategy is most likely to yield a usable first draft?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Attach the prior newsletter, and ask Claude to match its tone and structure while incorporating the new key messages for the three named regions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Attach the prior newsletter and the agreed key messages, and ask Claude to produce a similar newsletter for this quarter.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Provide the agreed key messages and the three regions, and ask Claude to choose an appropriate length and tone for store managers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Name the audience, the three regions, the length, the tone, and the agreed key messages, and reference the prior newsletter only as a tone example.

definition.explanation:
Clear, explicit instructions about the intended audience, regional scope, output length, tone, and required key messages give Claude the constraints needed to produce a suitable draft. A prior newsletter can effectively guide the requested tone without substituting for the current content requirements. Anthropic’s prompt-engineering guidance recommends clearly specifying the desired output and using relevant examples and details.

**Learn more:** [Claude 4 prompt engineering best practices](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-4-best-practices)

definition.stemRaw:
You are an HR specialist categorizing potential ethical risks in a Claude-supported workflow.  
  
Which two risks raise the greatest ethical concern in an HR-adjacent workflow? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer represents a complete solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: decisions that materially affect a person’s employment without human accountability

choices.label: B
choices.text: a clerical typo in a routine internal calendar invitation

choices.label: C
choices.text: inconsistent tone and formatting across internal HR communications sent to employees

choices.label: D
choices.text: inconsistent use of the company’s preferred dash style across documents

choices.label: E
choices.text: outputs that systematically disadvantage members of a protected group

definition.explanation: High-impact employment decisions require human accountability because they can materially affect a person’s livelihood. Outputs that systematically disadvantage a protected group create discriminatory harm and are therefore a critical ethical concern.

definition.stemRaw: You are an operations assistant asking Claude to summarize 200 weekly metric records across several regions. Which output format presents the data most clearly?

choices.label: A
choices.text: a bulleted list of observations grouped by region without consistent metrics across entries

choices.label: B
choices.text: a narrative summary organized by region, describing trends and notable records in prose

choices.label: C
choices.text: a series of regional narrative briefs, each describing weekly performance in paragraph form

choices.label: D
choices.text: a structured table with one record per row and one metric per column, sorted by region

definition.explanation: A structured table makes a large, multi-region dataset easy to scan, compare, sort, and analyze because records and metrics occupy consistent rows and columns.

definition.stemRaw: You are an analyst reviewing a Claude response that answers two of three required questions but omits the third. Which prompt element most likely needs to be strengthened?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The context provided to Claude should be expanded with additional background detail about the subject matter.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The output format should be revised to allow Claude to determine the appropriate structure for each question’s answer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The role assigned to Claude should be changed to a more specialized expert persona to increase response depth.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The task statement should explicitly enumerate the three required questions and require an answer to each.

definition.explanation: Explicitly enumerating the three required questions and directing Claude to answer each one makes task-completeness requirements unambiguous and reduces the risk that a required item is skipped.

definition.stemRaw:
An HR team member is reviewing a Claude-generated set of interview questions meant to be used with every candidate for one role. The questions will be asked in the same sequence to each candidate.  
  
Which review practice best promotes fairness?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Review the questions to ensure they apply equally to all candidates, avoid assumptions about candidate backgrounds, and focus on the role’s actual requirements.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Review the questions for length and tone, since the questions Claude drafts are well-aligned to role requirements by default and need only stylistic adjustment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Review the questions and add follow-up questions tailored to each candidate’s resume so each interview can explore the candidate’s specific experience.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Review the questions and rotate the order across candidates so no candidate is consistently asked the hardest questions first.

definition.explanation:
Fair interview questions are job-related, avoid assumptions about protected or personal backgrounds, and can be applied consistently to every candidate. The EEOC identifies asking the same questions for a job and focusing inquiries directly on the position as practices that support nondiscriminatory treatment.

**Learn more:** [Barrier Analysis: Questions to Guide the Process](https://www.eeoc.gov/federal-sector/management-directive/barrier-analysis-questions-guide-process) · [Employment Tests and Selection Procedures](https://www.eeoc.gov/laws/guidance/employment-tests-and-selection-procedures)

definition.stemRaw: You are a marketing manager using Claude to research a new market segment. Which research step should be completed first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Generate a final research report combining every Claude output produced.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Submit a series of Claude prompts to gather information across the segment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Validate the gathered information against authoritative external sources.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Define the specific research questions that must be answered for the segment.

definition.explanation:
Research must begin by defining the specific questions to be answered, because they set the scope for information gathering, source validation, and the final report. Anthropic’s guidance likewise emphasizes clearly defining specific, measurable objectives before subsequent evaluation work.

**Learn more:** [Define success and build evaluations](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/develop-tests)

definition.stemRaw:
An HR business partner is setting up two separate Projects for two different client engagements.  
  
Which configuration most effectively prevents context bleed between the two engagements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set up each Project with its own distinct memory context, knowledge sources, and instructions, and verify that information from one Project does not appear in the other Project’s responses.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use a single shared Project for both client engagements with combined memory, knowledge sources, and instructions, on the assumption that Claude will keep the two clients’ contexts separate without configuration.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure both Projects to share the same memory context to reduce setup effort, even though shared memory between unrelated client engagements is precisely the configuration that produces context bleed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Skip Project configuration entirely and use general chats for both engagements, which provides no scoped memory contexts and offers no structural separation between the two clients’ work streams.

definition.explanation:
Separate Claude Projects provide self-contained workspaces with project-specific knowledge and instructions. Assigning distinct context, knowledge sources, and instructions to each client engagement preserves the boundary between their work and prevents one client’s information from being used in the other engagement.

**Learn more:** [What are projects? | Anthropic Help Center](https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/9517075-what-are-projects) · [How can I create and manage projects? | Anthropic Help Center](https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/9519177-how-can-i-create-and-manage-projects)

definition.stemRaw:
You are an operations assistant choosing a model for a recurring meeting-summary task that needs no deep reasoning and operates at moderate volume.  
  
Which choice best balances cost, speed, and quality?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Haiku, which is suitable only when the task requires the fastest possible turnaround.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Opus, which prioritizes depth at higher latency and rate-limit consumption.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sonnet, which provides solid quality at moderate latency and rate-limit consumption for everyday work.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A custom model, which the Associate-level user would need to build and train independently.

definition.explanation:
Sonnet is the balanced Claude model tier for routine work that needs solid output quality without the higher cost and latency associated with Opus. Haiku is optimized for simpler, high-speed and high-volume workloads, while Opus is intended for the most demanding reasoning tasks.

**Learn more:** [Anthropic pricing and cost optimization](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/about-claude/pricing) · [Anthropic Intro to Claude](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/welcome)

definition.stemRaw:
You are a project manager assessing Claude usage methods that teammates have proposed for a project workflow.  
  
Which two workflow steps are appropriate for Claude support? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer provides a complete solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: approving a final external press release without any human review

choices.label: B
choices.text: issuing legally binding contractual commitments on behalf of the company

choices.label: C
choices.text: deciding promotion outcomes for staff based solely on the model’s judgment

choices.label: D
choices.text: synthesizing a literature review across many uploaded research documents

choices.label: E
choices.text: drafting a structured project status update from a set of meeting notes

definition.explanation: Claude can synthesize information across uploaded research documents to support a literature review and can turn meeting notes into a structured project-status-update draft. These are assistive drafting and summarization tasks that remain subject to human review, unlike autonomous final press approval, legally binding commitments, or sole-model employment decisions.

definition.stemRaw:
You are an operations lead aligning production tasks with Claude’s model strengths to establish realistic expectations.  
  
Which two production tasks most clearly match Claude’s strengths? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer represents a complete solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: monitoring a live sensor data stream and flagging anomalies as they occur in real time

choices.label: B
choices.text: issuing a binding legal determination based solely on Claude’s analysis of case documents

choices.label: C
choices.text: drafting a tone-and-audience-aware customer-facing email under human review

choices.label: D
choices.text: calculating the precise settlement value of a derivative contract using live market inputs

choices.label: E
choices.text: synthesizing a single executive summary across many long source documents

definition.explanation:
Claude is designed for language and analysis tasks, including generating text and summarizing source material. It can draft a customer-facing email using specified tone and audience requirements under human review, and its large context capacity supports synthesizing an executive summary from numerous long documents. Binding legal judgments, exact financial settlement calculations using live inputs, and real-time anomaly detection require specialized controls, authoritative data, or deterministic and accountable decision processes beyond those language-model strengths.

**Learn more:** [Intro to Claude](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/welcome) · [Citations](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/citations)

definition.stemRaw:
A learning specialist is setting up a Project for course-design work. The organization has an internal instructional-design standard and a preferred format for lesson outlines.  
  
Which set of custom instructions best supports this use case?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Name Claude’s role as a course designer; let each chat’s prompt specify the standards and output structure for that lesson, since lessons vary widely.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Name Claude’s role as a course designer and require alignment to the organization’s instructional-design standards; leave output structure to Claude based on the topic of each lesson.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Specify only the preferred output structure for lesson outlines, since the structure carries the standards implicitly and naming the role adds no value.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Name Claude’s role as a course designer, require alignment to the organization’s instructional-design standards, and specify the preferred output structure for lesson outlines.

definition.explanation:
Project instructions apply to all chats within a Project and are intended to establish project-specific context, workflow guidelines, task requirements, and the role or perspective Claude should adopt. Including the course-designer role, the organization’s instructional-design standards, and the required lesson-outline structure provides consistent guidance for every lesson.

**Learn more:** [Understanding Claude's Personalization Features](https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/10185728-understanding-claude-s-personalization-features) · [How can I create and manage projects?](https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/9519177-how-can-i-create-and-manage-projects)

definition.stemRaw:
You are a project manager evaluating stakeholder messages that teammates have drafted regarding Claude’s role in a workflow. Which two messages are appropriate for stakeholder communication about Claude? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer represents part of the solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: a claim that the model never makes errors and requires no quality review

choices.label: B
choices.text: a vague reassurance that “the AI is taking care of it” without further detail

choices.label: C
choices.text: a claim that Claude will handle every task without any human involvement

choices.label: D
choices.text: a clear statement of the limits and known failure modes of the integration

choices.label: E
choices.text: an honest description of where Claude assists and where humans retain decisions

definition.explanation:
Claude can generate factually incorrect or contextually inconsistent output, and mitigation techniques do not eliminate that risk; critical information still requires validation. Appropriate stakeholder communication therefore states the integration’s limitations and known failure modes, while honestly defining Claude’s assistance role and the decisions that remain with humans.

**Learn more:** [Reduce hallucinations — Claude Platform Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-hallucinations)

definition.stemRaw:
You are reviewing a competitor brief generated by Claude for unsupported claims.  
  
What is the correct sequence of review steps?  
  
1. Cross-check each specific claim against the provided source material or reliable external references.  
2. Determine whether to correct, re-prompt, or escalate based on the findings.  
3. Record every unsupported or inconsistent claim with its location and severity.  
4. Identify the specific factual claims, statistics, and citations in the brief.  
5. Read the brief from start to finish and flag any claims that seem surprising.
definition.explanation: An effective unsupported-claim review starts with a complete read-through to spot potentially questionable content, followed by identifying the exact claims, statistics, and citations requiring validation. Those items are then checked against authoritative evidence, documented when unsupported or inconsistent, and used to determine the appropriate remediation or escalation.

definition.stemRaw:
You are creating a checklist to evaluate Claude outputs and must finish the upstream steps before scoring an output. Which two steps must be completed **BEFORE** scoring a Claude output against the checklist? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer represents part of the solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Define the evaluation criteria that matter for the task at hand.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Promote the approved output into the downstream production process.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Forward unacceptable outputs to a senior reviewer for second-pass review.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Specify the threshold that distinguishes acceptable from unacceptable output.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Document the final score and the reviewer comments for the audit trail.

definition.explanation: An evaluation checklist requires task-relevant criteria to determine what quality dimensions are assessed and an acceptance threshold to determine whether the assessed output passes. Those definitions must exist before any score can be assigned; production routing, escalation, and audit recording are downstream activities.

definition.stemRaw:
You are a business analyst determining which output-formatting and context-window practices to recommend to teammates. Which two practices constitute effective use of the context window? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer provides part of the solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reuse the same context block across multiple requests to avoid rebuilding it each time.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Concatenate all source documents end-to-end with no separators between them.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Paste full email threads related to the project into context so the model has complete conversational history.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trim irrelevant material before submitting the request to keep context focused.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Use clear section headers to separate different parts of the input material.

definition.explanation:
A context window has finite input capacity, so removing irrelevant content keeps the available tokens focused on information needed for the task. Clear section headers delineate separate input materials and make their relationships and purposes easier for the model to interpret. Oversized inputs can otherwise require truncation or fail when they exceed the model’s input limit.

**Learn more:** [OpenAI API Reference — Responses truncation](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses-streaming/response/refusal?lang=python) · [OpenAI API — Models](https://platform.openai.com/docs/models/gpt-4-turbo-and-gpt-4)

definition.stemRaw:
When preparing an AI-assisted work product for external delivery, a senior manager is applying the AI Fluency Framework’s Diligence competency.  
  
Which step most clearly reflects Diligence principles?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deliver the work product without independent verification on the basis that AI assistance shifts accountability away from the human, even though Diligence holds the human fully accountable for the output.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Delegate accountability for the AI-assisted work product to Claude itself rather than retaining it as a human obligation, contrary to the Diligence principle that humans remain accountable for AI-assisted outputs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Skip verification of any element on the assumption that fluent output implies accuracy, even though Diligence requires the human to verify and correct AI-assisted outputs before they are acted upon.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Identify the elements of the work product that must be independently verified or corrected before delivery, and take ownership of those verifications as a professional accountability obligation.

definition.explanation:
Deployment Diligence requires the human using AI to verify and vouch for outputs that will be used or shared. Professional accountability remains with the human, so identifying what needs independent verification or correction and personally owning those checks before external delivery fulfills the requirement.

**Learn more:** [Anthropic AI Fluency: Diligence](https://www.anthropic.com/ai-fluency/due-dilligence?vid=240)

definition.stemRaw:
You are reviewing colleagues’ claims from a recent training about prompt iteration. Which two claims about prompt iteration are accurate? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer provides a complete solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Repeated resubmission of the same prompt is the most reliable way to improve output.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Output comparison against original criteria validates whether iteration helped.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Iteration is most productive when each change targets a specific diagnosed weakness.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Iteration should stop only after every possible alternative phrasing has been tried.

choices.label: E
choices.text: More iterations always produce a better output regardless of what was changed.

definition.explanation: Prompt iteration should be guided by explicit evaluation criteria: comparing revised output with the original criteria shows whether the change helped. Iterations are most effective when each revision addresses a specific identified weakness, rather than making arbitrary or repeated changes.

definition.stemRaw:
A Claude associate is examining Claude-generated customer-segment descriptions for an internal marketing brief. One description makes a generalization about a demographic group’s purchasing behavior that is not true for individual customers within that segment.  
  
Which response is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Revise the description to focus on observed behaviors rather than generalizations about people, and validate the revision against actual customer data.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Remove the entire customer-segment description from the brief, since any segmentation that involves demographic characteristics is likely to introduce similar issues.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Keep the description as written for the internal brief, since internal use does not carry the same risk as external publication of demographic generalizations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add a disclaimer to the description, noting that the generalization may not apply to all individuals in the segment, and keep the underlying description unchanged.

definition.explanation: Customer segmentation should describe demonstrable customer behaviors and be validated against actual customer data, rather than applying an unsupported demographic generalization to individuals. A disclaimer or internal-only use does not correct the inaccurate underlying characterization.

definition.stemRaw:
You are conducting an optimization pass on a recurring workflow.  
  
What is the correct sequence of optimization steps?  
  
1. Apply targeted optimization to the bottleneck step  
2. Roll out the optimized workflow to the wider team and document the change  
3. Identify the bottleneck step by using measured time per step and queue length  
4. Map the existing workflow steps, owners, and decision points  
5. Pilot the change with a small group and measure its effect against the previous baseline
definition.explanation: Workflow optimization begins by mapping the current process, then using performance measurements to identify the bottleneck. A targeted improvement is applied to that constraint, tested in a limited pilot against the established baseline, and only then rolled out broadly with documentation.

definition.stemRaw: You are a customer-success lead operating an interactive workflow in which every turn must respond quickly and the reasoning required per turn is light. Which option best matches these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Choose any model because latency does not vary by model.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Choose Haiku to keep latency low and to handle a light reasoning load efficiently at scale.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Choose Opus to maximize reasoning depth despite higher latency.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Choose a model based on the alphabetical order of its name.

definition.explanation:
Haiku is the appropriate model family for simple, high-volume, latency-sensitive work. Anthropic’s guidance recommends using Haiku for simple tasks and reserving more capable models for complex reasoning, so it aligns with fast interactive turns that need only light reasoning.

**Learn more:** [Anthropic pricing and cost optimization guidance](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/about-claude/pricing)

definition.stemRaw: As part of a workflow redesign, a process analyst is applying the AI Fluency Framework’s Delegation competency. Which two criteria most directly guide Delegation decisions? (Choose two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The reversibility of the task and the consequence of an error, which together indicate whether the step is safe to delegate to Claude or should be retained for human decision-making.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The need for human creativity, empathy, or judgment in the step, which indicates whether the task is appropriate for AI delegation or requires the human capabilities Claude cannot provide.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The visual complexity of the workflow diagram, since steps with more connections and dependencies are more likely to require human oversight.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The seniority of the team member who currently performs the step, since more senior roles typically involve higher-stakes tasks that warrant human retention.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The length of time the workflow has existed in its current form, since well-established processes have been sufficiently validated for AI delegation.

definition.explanation:
Delegation strategically divides work between humans and AI based on the nature and stakes of each task. Error consequence and reversibility determine whether delegation is acceptably safe, while tasks requiring human expertise, creativity, empathy, or judgment should remain human-led. The AI Fluency Framework specifically identifies human expertise, creativity, and judgment as considerations when distributing work between people and AI.

**Learn more:** [Anthropic AI Fluency: Delegation](https://www.anthropic.com/ai-fluency/ai-fluency-delegation)

definition.stemRaw: A Claude associate is assessing whether to enable a Skill supplied by an unfamiliar third party. Which two checks best support a sound trust decision? (Choose two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Verify the source of the Skill against the organization’s approved-Skill list before enabling it within claude.ai or any Project the team uses for its work.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Treat the Skill's appearance in a public listing as sufficient validation, without confirming the source, the requested permissions, or alignment with the organization’s approved-Skill list.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Skip permission review on the assumption that the Skill cannot exceed the boundaries of the workflow, even though Skills can request access that the task does not require.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Review the permissions and capabilities the Skill requests and confirm that the requested access is appropriate for the task the Skill is intended to perform.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Enable the Skill immediately on the basis of strong external reviews, even though the source has not been validated against the organization’s approved-Skill list and the permissions remain unverified.

definition.explanation:
Third-party Skills should be enabled only from trusted, organization-approved sources, and their requested capabilities and access should be reviewed to ensure they are necessary and appropriate for the intended task. Public listings or favorable reviews do not substitute for validating provenance and applying least-privilege access.

**Learn more:** [Use skills in Claude](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512180-use-skills-in-claude)

definition.stemRaw:
You are a research associate assembling inputs for a lengthy task that refers to two long regulatory documents, but only particular sections are relevant.  
  
Which approach best preserves context-window capacity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Skip the documents entirely and rely on Claude to invent the missing context.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Split each document into one-character pieces and feed them one at a time.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Extract only the relevant sections from each document and include those, omitting unrelated chapters.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Paste the full text of both documents without trimming to maximize available material.

definition.explanation: Extracting and supplying only the relevant sections retains the necessary regulatory context while avoiding token consumption by unrelated chapters, preserving more context-window capacity for the task.

definition.stemRaw: You are a project lead evaluating a teammate’s practice of using the same prompt template for every task, regardless of task type. Which feedback is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The prompting strategy should be adapted to each task type because one template does not produce equally strong outputs across all tasks.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The habit is ideal because a single template guarantees consistent quality across all task types.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The prompting strategy should not change between tasks because adapting it wastes time and adds no value.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Task type has no effect on the appropriate prompting strategy.

definition.explanation: Prompting strategy should be adapted to the task type because different tasks require different instructions, context, output formats, constraints, and evaluation criteria. A single template cannot reliably produce equally strong results across every type of task.

definition.stemRaw:
You are a knowledge worker preparing a summary of common prompt-failure patterns for the team.  
  
Which pattern is most likely to result in vague or off-target output?

choices.label: A
choices.text: a prompt that names a topic but does not state the task, audience, or required output structure

choices.label: B
choices.text: a prompt that adds clear constraints on length and tone

choices.label: C
choices.text: a prompt that explicitly names the role, task, audience, and required output format

choices.label: D
choices.text: a prompt that includes a representative example of the desired output

definition.explanation: A prompt that identifies only a topic leaves the intended task, audience, and response structure undefined. Those missing constraints force the model to infer essential requirements, increasing the likelihood of a generic or misaligned response.

definition.stemRaw:
You are an HR specialist assessing data items proposed for inclusion in a Claude prompt. Which two data items are suitable to include in a Claude prompt for a routine task? **(Choose two.)**  
  
Each correct answer provides a complete solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: a redacted job description that the model will adapt for a posting

choices.label: B
choices.text: accommodation request notes from an employee’s HR file needed to draft a role adjustment memo

choices.label: C
choices.text: employee ID numbers and hire dates for the team roster included to help Claude personalize onboarding communications

choices.label: D
choices.text: a compensation band summary that includes employee names and current salary figures for a specific team

choices.label: E
choices.text: an anonymized summary of an HR policy that the model will rephrase

definition.explanation: A redacted job description and an anonymized HR-policy summary are appropriately minimized and do not contain identifiable or sensitive employee information. Employee accommodation records, identifiers and hire dates, and named salary information are confidential HR data and are unsuitable for routine prompting.

definition.stemRaw:
You are a Claude associate evaluating a proposed Claude use case before approving it for your team. What is the correct sequence of assessment steps?  
  
1. Identify the audience, decision impact, and reversibility of the outputs.  
2. Identify the data types involved and whether sensitive data is implicated.  
3. Compare the use case with the organization’s policies and the relevant regulatory considerations.  
4. Decide whether the use case proceeds, needs modification, or is declined.  
5. Document the assessment outcome and rationale for traceability.

Claude’s first output is partly useful, but it has issues with tone and detail.  
  
Which two refinement actions are most likely to result in a meaningfully better output? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer provides a complete solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Provide an example of an output that meets the desired standard.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Append the phrase “please do better” to the end of the original prompt.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add a specific tone descriptor and a concrete audience to the prompt.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase the temperature setting and resubmit the unchanged prompt.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Resubmit the same prompt several times and select the best response.

definition.explanation:
A representative example gives Claude a concrete standard for the desired response, including its tone and level of detail. Explicitly naming the desired tone and a specific audience also supplies actionable constraints that guide style, vocabulary, and appropriate depth. Anthropic recommends clear, explicit instructions and notes that Claude pays attention to details and examples.

**Learn more:** [Claude 4 prompt engineering best practices](https://docs.anthropic.com/zh-CN/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-4-best-practices)

definition.stemRaw:
You are reviewing colleagues’ replies to feedback received on communications drafted by Claude. Which two feedback responses are productive? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer represents a complete solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: declining to revise sections that were generated by Claude on the basis that the model’s output should be trusted as written

choices.label: B
choices.text: incorporating all feedback received, including contradictory suggestions, into the next draft simultaneously

choices.label: C
choices.text: deferring all feedback to a later revision cycle to avoid disrupting the current draft’s consistency

choices.label: D
choices.text: asking clarifying questions when feedback is ambiguous before acting on it

choices.label: E
choices.text: mapping each piece of feedback to the specific change made in the next draft

definition.explanation:
Ambiguous feedback should be clarified before it is applied so that revisions reflect the reviewer’s intended meaning. Linking every feedback item to its corresponding change creates an auditable revision trail and helps confirm that feedback has been addressed. Claude-generated content should still be reviewed and verified rather than treated as automatically correct.

**Learn more:** [Reduce hallucinations — Claude Platform Docs](https://docs.anthropic.com/zh-CN/docs/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-hallucinations)

definition.stemRaw:
A project manager is determining how Claude can assist with requirements analysis for an upcoming engagement. The team will conduct stakeholder interviews and review existing process documentation during discovery.  
  
Which activity fits this domain?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use Claude to generate a complete requirements list from the project name and a short description, since requirements for similar engagements are largely standard.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use Claude to prioritize the requirements the team has already gathered, leaving the gathering itself to manual analyst work since prioritization is more time-consuming.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use Claude to synthesize stakeholder inputs and existing process documentation into a structured list of requirements with traceability to each source.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use Claude to conduct the stakeholder interviews directly, with the analyst reviewing the recordings afterward to confirm the requirements Claude extracted.

definition.explanation:
Claude can synthesize information from stakeholder interviews and process documents into a structured requirements set. Source traceability makes each requirement auditable against the underlying input, helping analysts validate the result and reduce unsupported claims. Anthropic’s documentation supports analyzing supplied documents and generating citations that point to specific source locations.

**Learn more:** [Citations - Anthropic Documentation](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/citations) · [Intro to Claude - Anthropic Documentation](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/welcome)

definition.stemRaw:
An account manager used Claude to extract requirements from stakeholder notes. Three requirements seem to be in conflict: two stakeholders specified mutually exclusive workflow steps, and a third requirement presumes an outcome that the first two would prevent.  
  
Which action is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Present all three conflicting requirements as alternative options in the requirements document, leaving the resolution to the project’s decision-making process later.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Apply Claude to propose a compromise wording for each conflict and submit the compromise to stakeholders as the proposed resolution.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Select the requirement that has the strongest business justification in the source notes, set the conflicting requirements aside, and proceed with the selected one.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Flag the conflicts in the requirements document, document the source for each side, and route the conflicts back to the originating stakeholders for resolution.

definition.explanation: Requirements conflicts should be explicitly documented with traceability to each originating source and returned to the relevant stakeholders for resolution. This preserves accountability and prevents an analyst or AI tool from making an unauthorized business decision.

definition.stemRaw: A knowledge worker is describing the cost, speed, and quality trade-offs among Claude models to a colleague. Which generalization accurately characterizes this trade-off?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Speed and rate-limit consumption are independent of model capability; the difference between Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus is reasoning depth alone.

choices.label: B
choices.text: More capable models generally consume more of the rate limit and run more slowly, while lighter models are faster and consume less of the rate limit.

choices.label: C
choices.text: More capable models generally consume less of the rate limit because their reasoning is more efficient, even though they run more slowly than lighter models.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lighter models consume more of the rate limit per request than more capable models, since lighter models require multiple passes to match heavier-model quality.

definition.explanation:
Claude’s model lineup generally trades efficiency for capability: lighter models such as Haiku are intended for simpler, fast, lower-cost work, while more capable models such as Sonnet and Opus are used for more complex reasoning and have higher token pricing and resource consumption. This supports the general pattern of greater rate-limit use and slower execution for more capable models.

**Learn more:** [Anthropic Pricing](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/about-claude/pricing)

definition.stemRaw: A finance manager needs to choose a Claude feature for work requiring deterministic calculations across a multi-tab spreadsheet. Which option best meets this requirement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use an Artifact alone for the calculations, which provides a stable editable surface for the result but does not perform the deterministic computation that Code Execution would run.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use Code Execution, which runs code in a sandbox to perform calculations on the uploaded file and produce verified outputs the associate can check.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use the Research feature for the calculations, which gathers and synthesizes external sources and is not the appropriate feature for deterministic computation on an uploaded spreadsheet.

choices.label: D

definition.explanation:
Claude Code Execution can run code in a secure sandbox, process uploaded files, and perform complex calculations. That makes it the appropriate feature for reproducible computations across a multi-tab spreadsheet.

definition.stemRaw:
A Claude associate is investigating a Claude response that answered only one of three required questions in a prompt. The prompt presented all three questions in one paragraph, separated by commas.  
  
Which root cause is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The prompt was too long and Claude focused on the question with the strongest grounding in the surrounding context.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The prompt’s required questions were addressed implicitly across the response, even though the response did not visibly answer each question.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The prompt’s task statement did not enumerate the three required questions explicitly enough for Claude to address each one in turn.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The prompt’s audience and tone specification overshadowed the task statement, so Claude prioritized voice over coverage.

definition.explanation: When a prompt contains several required items, explicitly numbering or otherwise enumerating each item makes the required coverage unambiguous and helps ensure that each is answered in sequence. Combining all three questions into a comma-separated paragraph leaves the task structure insufficiently explicit.

definition.stemRaw:
A sales manager is refining a Claude-generated solution prototype after a stakeholder review identified two particular concerns. The remainder of the prototype was approved as written.  
  
Which iteration approach is most likely to create a strong next version?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rewrite the prototype from scratch incorporating the two specific concerns, since starting fresh integrates the feedback more cleanly than targeted edits.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Address the two specific concerns and add a third improvement the associate identified, since combining stakeholder feedback with self- identified improvements is more efficient.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Address the two specific concerns directly, leave unrelated parts unchanged, and document the changes for the next review.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Address the two specific concerns and also revise unrelated sections to maintain consistent voice across the prototype after the edits.

definition.explanation: A focused revision incorporates the specific stakeholder feedback while retaining content that was already accepted. Documenting the changes also makes the subsequent review clearer and more traceable.

definition.stemRaw:
As a senior analyst, you use Claude to analyze requirements from several stakeholder sources.  
  
What is the correct sequence of steps?  
  
1. Group related requirements and flag conflicts or ambiguities for stakeholder review.  
2. Validate the structured output against the original sources for accuracy and completeness.  
3. Submit the consolidated inputs to Claude using a structured extraction prompt.  
4. Gather and label the source materials so that every requirement can be traced.  
5. Document the final requirements set with source traceability and status.
definition.explanation:
Source materials must be gathered and labeled before consolidation so each requirement remains traceable. The consolidated material is then submitted to Claude with a structured extraction prompt; the extracted requirements can subsequently be grouped and reviewed for conflicts or ambiguities. Validation against the original sources must occur before documenting the final, traceable requirements set. Anthropic’s citations documentation supports providing documents to Claude and retaining source references for verification.

**Learn more:** [Anthropic Claude Platform Docs: Citations](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/citations)

definition.stemRaw: You are assessing whether a request to “redesign new-hire onboarding” should be broken into parts before prompting Claude. Which characteristic of the request most strongly suggests that decomposition would be useful?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The request is for a single structured document that can be produced from one set of inputs in one prompt.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The request requires multiple distinct outputs: a process map, supporting materials, and a measurement plan.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The request involves a single well-defined output with a clear input and a familiar format.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The request involves content the associate has produced many times before and knows can be handled in a single well-structured prompt.

definition.explanation:
Decomposition is most valuable when work contains multiple distinct deliverables that require different kinds of content and evaluation. A process map, supporting materials, and a measurement plan are separate outputs, so treating them as coordinated subtasks improves clarity and control.

**Learn more:** [Customer Support Agent - Anthropic](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/about-claude/use-case-guides/customer-support-chat)

definition.stemRaw: You are a procurement associate breaking down a vendor-evaluation task. Which dependency sequence represents sound ordering?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Define evaluation criteria first, gather vendor data against those criteria, then score and rank.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Rank vendors before any data is collected.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Score vendors first and decide on the criteria afterward.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Skip criteria and ask Claude to produce a vendor recommendation from no inputs.

definition.explanation: A defensible vendor evaluation defines the assessment criteria before collecting evidence, then gathers vendor information aligned to those criteria, and finally uses that information to score and rank the vendors.

definition.stemRaw:
You are a marketing manager using Claude to develop ideas for a campaign and must complete the framing steps before generating concepts. Which two framing steps must be completed BEFORE asking Claude to generate concepts? (Choose two.)  
  
Each correct answer represents part of the solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Select a finalist concept and prepare it for stakeholder approval.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Define the goal of the campaign and the success metrics for the campaign.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Review the Claude-generated concepts and select the two strongest for further development.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Schedule the campaign launch and the rollout dates with the agency.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Define the brand voice and the audience the concepts will speak to.

definition.explanation:
Campaign ideation should begin with a clear objective and measurable success metrics, plus the target audience and brand voice that constrain relevance, tone, and style. Concept review, finalist selection, approval preparation, launch scheduling, and rollout planning take place after concepts have been generated.

**Learn more:** [Define success criteria and build evaluations — Claude Platform Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/it/test-and-evaluate/develop-tests) · [Prompting best practices — Claude Platform Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/ko/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices)

definition.stemRaw:
You are a knowledge worker determining whether to escalate Claude-generated output. What is the correct sequence of decision steps?  
  
1. Identify the audience and the impact if the output is incorrect.  
2. Document the decision and its rationale for traceability.  
3. Compare the output’s risk profile with the organization’s escalation criteria.  
4. Decide whether to use the output, iterate further, or escalate.  
5. Evaluate the output’s accuracy, completeness, and any unverified claims.
definition.explanation:
Assessing the audience and consequences establishes the potential impact, while evaluating accuracy, completeness, and unverified claims establishes the output’s quality risk. Those factors can then be measured against organizational escalation criteria before selecting use, iteration, or escalation; recording the decision and rationale provides traceability. Claude outputs can contain factual errors or unsupported claims, so critical and high-stakes information requires validation.

**Learn more:** [Reduce hallucinations — Claude Platform Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-hallucinations)

definition.stemRaw: You are a product designer using Claude in a solution-design exercise. Which solution-design step should be completed first when using Claude?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Articulate the problem the solution must address and the constraints in play.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Compare the candidate concepts against the constraints and select a finalist.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Produce detailed mock-ups of the chosen solution for stakeholder review.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Generate candidate solution concepts using Claude across diverse styles.

definition.explanation:
Defining the problem to solve and the applicable constraints establishes the goals, boundaries, and evaluation criteria for subsequent concept generation. Candidate concepts can then be generated, assessed against those constraints, selected, and developed into detailed mock-ups. Anthropic’s prompting guidance recommends clear, explicit instructions and relevant context so Claude can produce targeted results.

**Learn more:** [Claude 4 Prompt Engineering Best Practices — Anthropic](https://docs.anthropic.com/zh-CN/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-4-best-practices)
